intuition: A simulation is a controlled experiment on a model. A theorem must cover every case allowed by its assumptions.
learningGoal: Explore AI-assisted mathematical physics, fluid equations, and why successful simulations cannot establish a universal theorem.
exerciseNote: Read the evidence comparison and change simulation assumptions on paper; no laboratory or GPU is required.

quiz.question: Imagine an AI system produces one million successful simulations of fluid flow without encountering a singularity. Can we conclude that the Navier–Stokes equations always produce smooth solutions?
quiz.explanation: No. Simulations supply evidence for the cases examined. A universal smoothness claim needs a mathematical proof covering the conditions specified by the theorem.
